feature.title: Model Usage Tracking — Token and cost reporting via hermoso usage
feature.objective: Provide a hermoso usage CLI command that reads token and cost data from the hermes-telemetry SQLite database (~/.hermes/telemetry/telemetry.db), aggregates it by model, date, feature, and run, and displays it with optional JSON output. Local models report tokens with $0.00 cost. Pre-plugin sessions receive a coarse backfill estimate from session metadata.

requirements.title: Default output shows today's usage only
requirements.statement: Running hermoso usage with no flags shall display token counts and costs for the current calendar day, grouped by model. Local models shall show $0.00 cost.
requirements.rationale: The most common query is 'how much did I use today?' — this minimizes friction.

requirements.title: Date range filtering via --from and --to flags
requirements.statement: The --from and --to flags shall accept ISO 8601 date strings (YYYY-MM-DD) and filter telemetry rows to the inclusive date range.
requirements.rationale: Date ranges enable weekly and monthly reporting without requiring SQL knowledge.

requirements.title: Model filtering via --model flag
requirements.statement: The --model flag shall filter results to rows matching the given model name substring (case-insensitive).
requirements.rationale: Users with multiple models want to isolate costs per model.

requirements.title: Feature attribution via --feature flag
requirements.statement: The --feature flag shall filter results to sessions attributed to the given Hermoso feature ID via time-window overlap with run.created_at/updated_at.
requirements.rationale: Feature-level cost tracking requires mapping telemetry sessions to Hermoso runs.

requirements.title: Run attribution via --run flag
requirements.statement: The --run flag shall filter results to sessions attributed to the given Hermoso run ID via time-window overlap.
requirements.rationale: Run-level cost tracking supports per-increment billing questions.

requirements.title: Machine-readable JSON output via --json
requirements.statement: The --json flag shall emit structured JSON matching the standard Hermoso output envelope (ok, command, data) with a usage array containing model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost, and attribution fields.
requirements.rationale: JSON output enables scripting and dashboard integration.

requirements.title: Local model cost reported as $0.00
requirements.statement: For telemetry rows where cost is NULL or the model is served locally (cost absent from provider pricing), the CLI shall display $0.00 — explicit zero, not absent or 'N/A'.
requirements.rationale: Explicit zero confirms the row was processed and the cost is known to be zero, not missing.

requirements.title: Graceful handling when telemetry database does not exist
requirements.statement: If ~/.hermes/telemetry/telemetry.db does not exist, hermoso usage shall print a clear message ('No telemetry data found. Install the hermes-telemetry plugin to begin tracking.') and exit with code 0.
requirements.rationale: The plugin is a prerequisite. The CLI must not error out or crash — it should guide the user to the next step.

requirements.title: Coarse backfill from session metadata
requirements.statement: For sessions predating hermes-telemetry installation, hermoso usage shall walk ~/.hermes/sessions/, extract session duration, model name, and start timestamp from session metadata, estimate token usage (duration × base tokens/sec per model), and label results as 'estimated' in output.
requirements.rationale: Complete historical data is valuable even if approximate. The 'estimated' label prevents confusion with precise telemetry data.

requirements.title: Time-window attribution for run/feature mapping
requirements.statement: When --feature or --run is specified, telemetry rows shall be attributed to Hermoso runs by checking whether the row's timestamp falls within [run.created_at, run.updated_at]. If multiple runs overlap, the row is attributed to all matching runs.
requirements.rationale: Time-window matching is coarse but correct for the estimation use case. It avoids requiring invasive session_id instrumentation in every skill.

requirements.title: SQLite driver is pure Go, no CGO
requirements.statement: The SQLite dependency shall be modernc.org/sqlite (or another pure-Go, CGO-free SQLite driver), not github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3 which requires CGO and a system libsqlite3.
requirements.rationale: Hermoso ships as a static binary. CGO breaks cross-compilation and adds system library dependencies. Pure-Go SQLite preserves the static binary property.

requirements.title: Run state records the intent-phase model
requirements.statement: When a run is started (or its design first persisted), the run records the model, provider, and base_url that conducted the intent (grilling) session, taken from the live session metadata. This makes intent-phase token cost attributable in hermoso usage via the phase attribution described in req-usage-by-phase.

requirements.title: Profiles gain an intent phase binding
requirements.statement: The Hermoso profile schema gains an optional 'intent' phase entry ({profile, capture}) alongside the existing phase bindings; profiles/default.yaml sets intent to a near-frontier cloud profile. The controller validates it like any other phase binding.

requirements.title: Runs carry a follow_through policy
requirements.statement: Run state carries follow_through: auto | gated (default auto). Under auto, after each human approval gate the controller proceeds to the next phase under that phase's bound profile without returning control to the user; under gated it stops at every transition. The policy can be flipped on a run at any time (hermoso follow-through <ctx> auto|gated --json).

requirements.title: Model re-binds to the phase profile at every transition
requirements.statement: Each phase transition re-resolves the target phase's profile and its model (provider, base_url, model id) and dispatches that phase's work under it; no phase inherits the previous phase's model by accident. The resolved model per phase is recorded on the run for cost attribution.

requirements.title: Usage report attributes cost by process phase
requirements.statement: hermoso usage gains --by-phase aggregation: intent-phase rows are attributed via the recorded intent model and the run's intent window; specification/orchestration rows via their phase bindings and phase time windows recorded at transitions.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given a telemetry database with today's usage rows, when the user runs hermoso usage with no flags, then today's token counts and costs are displayed grouped by model, and local models show $0.00.
Given a telemetry database with rows spanning 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31, when the user runs hermoso usage --from 2026-08-10 --to 2026-08-20, then only rows within that date range are displayed.
Given a telemetry database with rows for models 'qwen-3.8-27b' and 'deepseek-v4', when the user runs hermoso usage --model qwen, then only 'qwen-3.8-27b' rows are displayed.
Given a telemetry row at timestamp T that falls within run R's [created_at, updated_at] window for feature F, when the user runs hermoso usage --feature F, then that row is included in the output.
Given a telemetry row at timestamp T that falls within run R's time window, when the user runs hermoso usage --run R, then that row is included in the output.
When the user runs hermoso usage --json, the output is valid JSON with an 'ok' field, 'command' field set to 'usage', and a 'data.usage' array.
Given that ~/.hermes/telemetry/telemetry.db does not exist, when the user runs hermoso usage, then the CLI prints a message about installing hermes-telemetry and exits with code 0.
Given session metadata predating the telemetry database, when hermoso usage includes backfill data, then those rows are labeled 'estimated' in the output and not mixed with precise telemetry rows.
When hermoso is built, go tool link does not invoke a C compiler for any telemetry-related package, confirming no CGO dependency.
All tests in internal/telemetry/ pass with go test ./internal/telemetry/ -v.
Given a run started from a session whose model was X, when hermoso status is queried, then the run's intent record shows model X with provider and base_url.
Given profiles/default.yaml with an intent binding, when the controller loads the profile, then it validates the intent phase and exposes it to phase resolution.

Given follow_through=auto and a just-approved design, when the approval is recorded, then the controller proceeds to the next phase (dispatching its profile's model) without waiting for another user prompt.
Given follow_through=gated, when a phase completes, then the controller stops and returns control to the user at that transition.
Given a run in any phase, when the user runs hermeso follow-through ... gated (or auto), then subsequent transitions respect the new policy.
Given phase A ran on model M1 and phase B binds model M2, when the run transitions A to B, then phase B work is dispatched to M2 and the run records the per-phase model mapping.

Given a run with an intent window on a frontier model and construction on local models, when hermoso usage --by-phase runs, then cost is split by phase with intent at its recorded rate and local phases at $0.00.

business_vocabulary.definition: A single row in the hermes-telemetry SQLite database containing session_id, provider, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cost, and timestamp.

The method of mapping a telemetry row to a Hermoso run by checking whether the row's timestamp falls within the run's created_at..updated_at interval. Coarse but functional without requiring session_id instrumentation.

Estimated usage data derived from session metadata (duration × model tokens/sec) for sessions that predate hermes-telemetry installation. Labeled as 'estimated' to distinguish from precise telemetry data.

interaction_surfaces.title: hermoso usage CLI command
interaction_surfaces.description: New subcommand in cmd/hermoso/main.go. Accepts --feature, --run, --model, --from, --to, --json flags. Default output is today's usage grouped by model.

interaction_surfaces.title: internal/telemetry package
interaction_surfaces.description: New Go package providing TelemetryStore interface and SQLiteTelemetryStore implementation. Reads telemetry.db, performs time-window attribution, and returns aggregated usage structs.

interaction_surfaces.title: go.mod — modernc.org/sqlite dependency
interaction_surfaces.description: New dependency on modernc.org/sqlite (pure-Go SQLite driver). Added to go.mod via go get.

interaction_surfaces.title: Run state schema — intent record, follow_through, per-phase model map
interaction_surfaces.description: internal/state: run JSON gains intent {model,provider,base_url,window}, follow_through enum, phase_models map. Migration: absent fields default (follow_through=auto, no intent record).

interaction_surfaces.title: Profile schema — intent phase binding
interaction_surfaces.description: profiles/default.yaml + internal/profile loader: optional 'intent' phase {profile, capture}.

interaction_surfaces.title: Controller — follow-through + re-bind at transitions
interaction_surfaces.description: Controller approves/advances logic: on transition, resolve next phase profile, dispatch under it, record per-phase model; respect follow_through.

interaction_surfaces.title: hermoso follow-through CLI
interaction_surfaces.description: hermoso follow-through <project> <feature> <run> <repo> auto|gated --json flips the policy on a live run.

constraints: No changes to .hermoso state files — usage is read-only from telemetry.db and .hermoso/runs/
No new daemon or background process — the CLI reads and exits
Output must match Hermoso's standard envelope format (ok, command, data)
Must compile as a static binary (no CGO) — any SQLite driver must be pure Go
Telemetry lane remains read-only with respect to .hermoso state; only the governance lane writes run-state fields (intent record, follow_through, phase_models)
Run-state additions must be backward compatible: old run.json files without the new fields load with defaults (follow_through=auto, empty intent record)
Intent model recording relies on session metadata availability; when absent, the intent record is left empty and usage attribution falls back to time-window heuristics
non_goals: OpenRouter API integration for direct cost lookup
Session_id instrumentation in Hermoso skills (deferred to future increment)

decisions.decision: Overrides constitution principle V (Minimal Dependencies) — this feature requires a pure-Go SQLite driver (modernc.org/sqlite) to read the hermes-telemetry database at ~/.hermes/telemetry/telemetry.db.
decisions.rationale: hermes-telemetry stores data in SQLite. No Go-native alternative exists for reading SQLite databases. modernc.org/sqlite is pure Go (no CGO), preserves static binary property, and is widely used. The dependency is scoped to internal/telemetry/ only — no other package imports it.

decisions.decision: Attribution via time-window overlap rather than explicit session_id fields in run state
decisions.rationale: Adding session_id to run state requires instrumenting every Hermeso skill dispatch. This is invasive and better deferred to a future increment. Time-window overlap is correct for the estimation use case this feature targets.

decisions.decision: Coarse backfill from session duration metadata rather than session transcript parsing
decisions.rationale: Session transcript parsing is fragile (model-dependent formatting) and expensive (LLM calls). Duration × tokens/sec is a simple heuristic that provides useful estimates with a clear 'estimated' caveat.
mattn/go-sqlite3 requires CGO and a system libsqlite3, breaking Hermoso's static binary property. modernc.org/sqlite is a pure-Go translation of SQLite with no CGO dependency.

decisions.decision: Escape hatch: overrides this design's earlier constraint 'No schema changes to hermoso run state' — the governance lane adds intent record, follow_through, and phase_models to run state.
decisions.rationale: Per-phase model governance requires durable, per-run state; time-window attribution alone cannot know which model conducted intent or what policy applies. Defaults keep old runs loading.

decisions.decision: follow_through defaults to auto, not gated.
decisions.rationale: The user's stated workflow: after the grilling settles, the process should move through stages automatically; stopping at every transition recreates the manual-churn problem. Human approval gates (design, contract, release) remain mandatory in both modes.

decisions.decision: Intent phase is profile-bound but model-recorded, not model-forced.
decisions.rationale: The intent grilling happens in the user's live chat where they may pick any near-frontier model (Claude/GPT-class or upper Kimi/GLM/DeepSeek tiers). Hermoso records what was actually used rather than forcing a switch, keeping intent flexible and cost attribution truthful.

decisions.decision: Re-bind at every transition rather than session inheritance.
decisions.rationale: The failure mode being prevented: an entire feature built on the expensive intent model because nothing switched back. Explicit re-resolution per phase makes the tier policy mechanical.
